what_its_for: Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to fight bacterial infections. It is commonly used to treat ear infections, sinus infections, throat infections (like strep throat), bronchitis, urinary tract infections (UTIs), skin infections, and Lyme disease. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection.
how_to_take: Take cefuroxime exactly as your doctor prescribed. The tablet form should be taken WITH food to help your body absorb it better and to reduce stomach upset. Swallow tablets whole if possible, but they can be crushed and mixed with a small amount of food like applesauce if needed — be aware the tablets have a strong, bitter taste. If you are taking the liquid (suspension) form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided. Do NOT use a regular kitchen spoon. Finish ALL of your medication even if you start feeling better. Stopping early can allow bacteria to come back and become harder to treat.
dosing: Your dose depends on the infection being treated, your age, weight, and kidney function. Adults are commonly prescribed 250 mg to 500 mg twice daily (every 12 hours). Children's doses are based on their weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow the specific instructions on your prescription label. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor for guidance.
storage: Tablets: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Liquid suspension: Store in the refrigerator (do NOT freeze). The mixed liquid is good for 10 days — discard any unused portion after 10 days. Keep all medication out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (like Maalox or Mylanta) within 2 hours of your cefuroxime dose, as they may reduce how well the medicine works. Avoid alcohol during treatment as it may worsen side effects like stomach upset. Do not take cefuroxime if you have a known allergy to penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics without first talking to your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody (this could be a serious gut infection called C. diff); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; or seizures. Also call your doctor if your symptoms are not improving after 2 to 3 days of treatment, or if they get worse at any time.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting cefuroxime. However, it is very important to complete the full course of antibiotics as prescribed, even if you feel completely better before you finish. Stopping early can cause your infection to return and may make it harder to treat in the future.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Cefuroxime is generally considered safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding, but always let your doctor know before taking any medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney Problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney problems. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Dosing adjustments may be needed based on kidney function. Children: The liquid suspension form is often used for children. Doses are weight-based and determined by your doctor or pharmacist. Penicillin Allergy: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin, as there is a small chance of cross-reactivity with cefuroxime.
